newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Suria says no move to merge with MBf Cap.
newsitem.headline: Suria says no move to merge with MBf Cap.

text.p: Financial services firm Suria Capital Holdings Bhd said on Monday it has not been officially approached by another firm for a stake in the company as widely-speculated.
Suria, which owns Sabah Bank Bhd and Sabah Development Bank, was rumoured in the last few weeks as being stalked by MBf Capital, also a financial services company.
"We have heard of these rumours, but so far there's no official approach to us," Suria's general manager Zainie Abdul Aucasa told Reuters.
"I am speaking to you honestly, we are not aware," he said.
MBf Capital officials were not immediately available for comment.

But the company on May 6 denied there was any known reason for the unsually high trading volume in its shares, though it was aware of media speculation about a possible merger between itself and Suria.
"We are not aware of any other rumours or other conditions that exist," MBf Capital said then.
Dealers said the stocks of Suria and MBf Capital were again boosted on Monday by renewed speculation over the merger. "We heard MBf is buying a Sabah bank," said one dealer.
Around 0825 GMT, Suria was up six cents to 2.64 ringgit and top-active MBf Capital jumped 42 cents to 4.68.
